memos.headline: Rotation into defensives and cyclicals accelerating as mega-cap tech breaks down over the past month
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe: JPM, UNH, PG, and CAT are holding near 52-week highs with positive 4-week relative strength versus SPY, while MSFT, AMZN, NVDA, and GOOGL have all suffered sharp 4-week drawdowns of -5% to -13% and are losing relative strength badly. MSFT is the weakest name at -27.9% off its 52-week high, trading 13.9% below its 200-day mean with an RSI of 37—this is a broken trend, not a dip to buy. UNH stands out as the strongest chart in the group: +43.7% over 12 weeks, only 1.1% from its high, with 12-week relative strength of +31.5% vs SPY, though RSI at 67.9 and a +12.3% premium to the 50-day mean warn of near-term extension. CAT's 12-week +31.3% surge and 52-week +52% gain are impressive, but the +38% premium to the 200-day mean makes me cautious about chasing—I'd want a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. I'm most convicted on avoiding MSFT and on staying long JPM, which shows the cleanest risk-adjusted uptrend: near highs, moderate RSI of 64.9, low ATR of 2.04%, and strong 4-week relative strength of +7.8%.

views.note: Cleanest uptrend in the universe—only 4.2% from highs, RSI 64.9 not yet overbought, +7.8% 4w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess below the 200-day (~$307).
Dominant relative strength (+31.5% vs SPY over 12w) and near all-time highs, but RSI 67.9 and +12.3% above 50d mean suggest waiting for a pullback toward $380 before adding size.
Broken trend: -27.9% drawdown from 52w high, 13.9% below 200d mean, RSI 37, persistent negative relative strength; would need a reclaim of the 200-day (~$454) to reconsider.
RSI 34.8 is the lowest in the group, 6.4% below 50d mean, -9.9% 4w relative strength vs SPY—momentum is clearly negative; a close above $255 (near 50d) would change my view.
Quiet relative outperformance over 4 weeks (+5.7% vs SPY), low ATR of 2.20%, and RSI 60 suggest steady accumulation; 12w relative weakness (-10.2%) tempers conviction.
Monster 26w gain of +52% and only 3.2% from highs, but +38% above 200d mean is extremely stretched—prefer to wait for a retest of the 50d area before going long.
Flat on the week and sitting near the 50d mean, but -13% over 4 weeks and -12.1% relative strength vs SPY show distribution; need a reclaim of $230 to turn constructive.
Strong 12w relative strength (+4.8%) but sharp 4w selloff of -10.3% has pulled RSI to 42.4; sitting near the 50d mean, so this is a decision point—break below $345 and I'd avoid.
Holding above both moving averages with modest 12w outperformance, but -5.3% last week and RSI 44 suggest fading momentum; a break below the 50d (~$285) would flip me to avoid.
12-week relative strength of -18.9% vs SPY is the worst in the universe despite a strong 26w absolute gain; price is rolling over below the 50d mean with RSI 43—trend has turned.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Deliver Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with accelerating, durable earnings power and those showing margin erosion. NVDA's 2027Q1 print is staggering—$81.6B revenue (+85% YoY) with a 71.5% net margin and net income up 211% YoY on only $8.5B of total debt—making it the cleanest earnings story I can find. GOOGL posted $110B in revenue (+22% YoY) with net margin expanding to 56.9% and net income surging 81%, while carrying just $14.8B in debt, which signals operating leverage still has room to run. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% net margin, and UNH grew revenue only 2% with flat net income and $77.9B in debt—both profiles I want to avoid until the earnings trajectory inflects. CAT surprised me positively with 22% revenue growth and 27% net income growth at a 14.6% margin, though I need to see whether the backlog sustains before getting more constructive.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% on minimal debt—unmatched earnings power in the universe.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with 56.9% net margin and only $14.8B debt signals durable, expanding profitability.
Revenue +18% YoY, net margin 38.3%, and net income +23% with moderate $40B debt reflects consistent cloud-driven earnings compounding.
Net income surged 77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expanded to 16.7%, though $122.6B in total debt warrants monitoring.
Solid +17% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt load and slower earnings growth vs. peers keep me neutral pending services mix detail.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% are impressive, but $36.2B debt against $17.4B quarterly revenue and cyclical exposure limit conviction.
Steady 10% revenue growth and 33% net margin are respectable for a bank, but earnings growth of 12.6% is pedestrian relative to tech peers.
Defensive 18.5% margin and 7% revenue growth are fine but 4.3% net income growth barely keeps pace with inflation.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B on a 4.9% net margin is clear cash-flow compression; I'd need margin recovery above 8% to reconsider.
Revenue growth of just 2% with flat net income and $77.9B debt signals stalling earnings power; would revisit if margin expands above 7%.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% With Sticky Inflation and Rising Long Rates — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months despite 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and CPI is running at 3.8% YoY — well above target — which removes any near-term impetus to ease further. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10 bps over three months and flat YoY, so there is no urgency from the employment mandate either. What concerns me is the long end: the 10y yield has risen 21 bps over three months to 4.48%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 17 bps to just 40 bps, signaling the market is repricing term premium higher amid persistent inflation. This backdrop is unfriendly for high-multiple duration assets and modestly supportive for banks (steeper NIM from positive but narrowing curve) and defensive staples. A CPI print falling below 3% annualized or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing and rotate me back into growth.

views.note: High-multiple tech faces headwinds from rising 10y yields and a Fed unlikely to cut soon, but stable consumer spending limits downside.
Duration-sensitive growth name under pressure from 4.48% 10y yields; pause regime caps re-rating potential.
Highest-beta duration name in the universe; rising long rates and sticky 3.8% YoY CPI argue against paying up for forward earnings.
Positive 10y-2y spread of 40 bps supports NIM, stable labor market underpins credit quality, and a Fed pause keeps short-rate income elevated.
Stable macro with no recession signal is fine for energy demand, but rising real rates and no easing catalyst limit upside.
Defensive staple benefits from a late-cycle pause regime; pricing power helps offset 3.8% CPI, and lower beta cushions against rate volatility.
Cyclical bellwether faces mixed signals: labor market is solid but rising long rates and curve flattening hint at slowing momentum ahead.
Consumer-facing strength from low unemployment offsets valuation pressure from higher discount rates; net effect is balanced.
Ad-driven revenue tied to nominal GDP growth which sticky inflation supports, but multiple expansion is capped by 4.48% 10y yields.
Defensive healthcare benefits from pause regime and stable employment; less rate-sensitive than tech peers.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: GOOGL and CAT Momentum Stands Out While MSFT and NVDA Face Headwinds
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence as proxies for sentiment direction across the universe. GOOGL (+10.0%) and CAT (+9.9%) posted the strongest earnings-day pops, and both have seen continued corporate activity — GOOGL with a flurry of material agreements and board changes through June 11, and CAT with fresh Reg FD disclosure on June 11, suggesting management is actively shaping the narrative. MSFT's -3.9% earnings reaction and two subsequent officer departure filings signal a negative tone shift that I do not believe has fully washed out. NVDA's -1.8% post-earnings drop combined with two director departure filings in late April and early May raises governance-noise concerns, though the magnitude is modest. UNH's +7.0% earnings pop was the second-largest in the group and subsequent filings have been routine, which I read as a stabilizing positive tone after what had been a turbulent period for managed care.

views.note: Strongest earnings reaction at +10.0% followed by an unusually dense cluster of material agreements and board activity through June, signaling sustained positive narrative momentum.
The +9.9% earnings-day move was emphatic and the June 11 Reg FD disclosure suggests management is keeping the positive narrative alive.
A +7.0% earnings pop and only routine filings since suggest the positive tone reset is holding, though I have less conviction given the lack of incremental catalysts.
The -3.9% earnings reaction was the worst in the group and two officer departure filings since suggest internal churn that could sustain negative sentiment.
Mild -1.8% earnings miss reaction and two director departures create noise, but the magnitude is too small to warrant a directional call.
Solid +3.2% earnings pop but no incremental filings since late April; positive tone likely already priced.
Muted +0.8% earnings reaction and a new material debt obligation on June 10 create an ambiguous tone picture.
The -1.0% earnings reaction was modest and subsequent filings are routine; no clear sentiment signal either way.
Heavy filing cadence (six 8-Ks since April) is mostly governance housekeeping with no earnings reaction data, leaving sentiment unclear.
Modest +1.7% earnings pop and Reg FD disclosure are consistent with stable defensive tone, but no upside catalyst.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Falling Fast but Elevated Oil and Rising VIX Signal Residual Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 39% over three months to 257, suggesting the worst of the tariff/sanctions shock is behind us, yet the level remains historically elevated. WTI at $91.58 is up 5.5% over three months, consistent with ongoing energy-supply tightness—likely tied to sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ discipline—even as the one-month decline of nearly 10% hints at some demand softening or diplomatic progress. The VIX ticking up 5.8% over the past month to 19.44 while HY spreads stay tight at 2.78% tells me markets are pricing event risk (possibly new export-control rounds or China-related actions) without yet seeing credit stress. I have moderate conviction that names with heavy China/semiconductor exposure (NVDA, AAPL) carry asymmetric downside from any fresh export-control escalation, while energy and infrastructure plays (XOM, CAT) benefit structurally from the current supply-constrained, reshoring-oriented policy environment. A reversal in my view would require a clear US-China trade détente or a material rollback of semiconductor export restrictions.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls remain the key structural overhang; any tightening toward China would hit NVDA's data-center pipeline disproportionately.
Supply-chain concentration in China is a known risk but diversification to India/Vietnam provides partial offset; I lack specific policy triggers to go stronger either way.
WTI at $91.58 and sanctions-driven supply tightness support upstream margins; XOM's Reg FD filing in May likely addressed capital discipline in this environment.
Two Reg FD filings in the window suggest active investor communication around infrastructure/reshoring tailwinds; policy uncertainty decline supports capex recovery.
Three 8-K filings in six weeks may reflect regulatory or antitrust developments; geopolitical risk is secondary to domestic policy risk here.
Tight HY spreads and a positive yield curve support bank earnings, but flattening over the past month and sanctions-related compliance costs temper enthusiasm.

Avoid broken-trend tech (MSFT) and earnings-challenged names (XOM), and size down where analysts conflict (NVDA, UNH, CAT).
